headline: Russia's first 300,000 diesel tonnes are a 42% shot to post a loading by 16 October
deck: Trump announced more than 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel immediately under a temporary US waiver. 42% a named loading is posted by 16:00 UTC 16 October.
body: President Donald Trump said Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace, another 500,000 tonnes during the month of November, and 1,000,000 tonnes immediately thereafter, Al Jazeera reported, after a discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin. [E4] CBS News reported a Truth Social post as placing that third million tonnes in December. [E1] This paper's 8 October forecast covered leftover International Energy Agency March barrels, diesel first.
Russia would deliver an additional 3 million tonnes of fuel "within a short period of time," Al Jazeera reported the president as adding. [E5]

PBS described a deal to obtain diesel from Russia as a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. [E8]

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it "a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners," according to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington, PBS reported. [E9]
The Treasury Department announced Friday that it would temporarily waive sanctions on Russia's energy sector to "allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market." [E2]

In a statement from the Kremlin later Friday, Putin confirmed he and Trump spoke on the phone and that "Russia confirmed its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the American and global markets," and he was "confident this will have a positive impact on the entire global economy," CBS News reported. [E3] Al Jazeera reported the Kremlin as saying the Russian side "reaffirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and world markets." [E6]
The Kremlin said the call between Putin and Trump, which lasted an hour and half, covered large-scale economic initiatives, including Russian fuel supplies, Al Jazeera reported. [E7]

**The desk's reading.** There is a 42% probability that a named official source or named news outlet reports, by 16:00 UTC on 16 October 2026, that the first announced diesel step has been loaded onto tankers under the US Treasury energy-sector waiver announced on 9 October 2026. The 42% is the posted-report call. The physical loading of that first announced step is 50%. A path on which the cargo moves and no named report arrives by the deadline is priced at 8% and settles no. The start is the announced instrument: a temporary Treasury waiver and a three-step diesel calendar whose first step is immediate. That is a legal gate plus a promised flow, not cargo that has posted a landing. The prior is this paper's 8 October leftover-barrel call, where member support for completing March releases left the withdrawal undated. Treasury's temporary waiver and the confirmed call move the probability up, because US persons have a stated path and both capitals agreed that fuel was on the table. No named tanker, port or buyer, the Kremlin's readiness to supply oil and petroleum products without a diesel loading of that first step, and the two accounts of when the third million tonnes lands, move it down; the extra fuel is "within a short period of time." The competing reading is that Russian diesel already sails, Friday opened a US payment path, and that first step will appear as a permitted cargo this week. A named loading under the waiver would move the call up. A restatement of the calendar with no hull, or silence by the deadline, would move it down. A silent physical cargo still settles no.

**The next test.** A named official source or named news outlet reports, by 16:00 UTC on 16 October 2026, that the first announced diesel step has been loaded onto tankers under the US Treasury energy-sector waiver announced on 9 October 2026. That report confirms the waiver moved oil. Silence, or another restatement of the calendar with no loading, confirms the promise. No such report by that deadline settles no.

flashpoint.note: Treasury waived energy sanctions to allow Russian diesel. The first 300,000 tonnes have no named tanker.

dissent.argument:
Start is the announced instrument: a temporary Treasury waiver and a three-step diesel calendar whose first step is more than 300,000 tonnes immediately. That is a legal gate plus a promised volume, not a stem. Russian diesel already leaves ports. A presidential calendar is not a loading. The leftover-IEA March-barrel prior is the wrong analogue: that was a stock draw with member support and no date. This is a new US payment path laid over product that already sails without a waiver tag.

The confirmed call and Treasury's temporary waiver move a physical loading up, because US persons have a stated path and both capitals put fuel on the table. No named tanker, port or buyer, the Kremlin's readiness to supply oil and petroleum products without a diesel loading of that first step, and two clocks on the third million tonnes, move it down. Immediately was Friday. A 300,000-tonne diesel programme is several product-tanker stems; by this filing it still has no hull. The waiver is a temporary energy-sector gate, not a loading deadline. Zelenskyy's condemnation does not move tonnes.

I put the physical loading of that first step under the waiver at 35%. Foreman's 8% no-report path is close; I price silence at 7%, because a waiver-tagged 300,000 tonnes would be the story if it posted, and ordinary Russian diesel that is not labeled under the waiver still settles no. The posted-report call is 28%. Settlement is the same: a named report by 16:00 UTC on 16 October that at least 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel has been loaded onto tankers under the 9 October Treasury waiver. A named fixture or port loading under that license would move me up; another restatement of the calendar with no hull, or silence, would move me down.
